hints.title: Read the centre by completing squares
hints.body: Group the x-terms and the y-terms separately. Rewrite each group as a square plus a constant.
hints.recap: A circle equation can be written as two squared distances from its centre.
hints.pitfall: Add back both constants introduced by completing the squares.
hints.pause: Rewrite the whole equation in centre-radius form.

recall.reminder: The form <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math> gives centre <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and squared radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math>.

hints.title: Isolate the squared radius
hints.body: After moving the constant terms, the right-hand side is 2p2−8p. This is the squared radius, not the radius.
hints.recap: Whether a real circle exists is controlled by the sign of its squared radius.
hints.pitfall: A zero squared radius gives only one point.
hints.pause: Write the strict inequality the right-hand side must satisfy.

recall.reminder: Completing the square separates a squared variable from the expression controlling its possible values.

hints.title: Use the signs of the factors
hints.body: Factor your quadratic inequality. Mark its two zeros on a number line and determine the sign in each of the three intervals.
hints.recap: A product changes sign at a simple root; test each interval rather than choosing the interval between the roots automatically.
hints.pitfall: The endpoints must be checked against the strict circle condition.
hints.pause: Select the intervals that satisfy your inequality and compare the result with the options.

recall.reminder: A sign chart records where each factor is positive or negative.

solution:
Completing both squares gives (x−p)2+(y−3)2=2p2−8p=2p(p−4). A circle has a positive radius, so its squared radius must be strictly positive.

The product p(p−4) is positive outside its two zeros. Hence p<0 or p>4. At p=0 or p=4, the locus is a single point, not a circle.

Answer D.
knowledgePattern: Complete both squares and require a strictly positive squared radius
